display_name: E - Asymmetric: tight stop, distant target
thesis: This card is organised around the payoff shape, not the signal: a deliberately low win rate traded for a large reward-to-risk, so the edge lives in the few trades that become real trend continuations, not in being right often. The universe is ten early-stage AI-infrastructure/power/compute names (memory, networking optics, neocloud capacity, nuclear/fuel, crypto infra) whose re-ratings are lumpy rather than smooth: most sessions are noise around a range, but a real catalyst -- a capacity contract, a beat that resets estimates, a sector-wide re-rating -- can add 25-40%+ over a few weeks as sell-side models and momentum/CTA flow catch up with news that was already public. The entry (close > bb_upper(20,2) and macd_hist(12,26,9) > 0 and close > sma(50)) tries to catch that catalyst near its start -- a statistically unusual band breakout, confirmed by accelerating momentum, inside an already-established uptrend -- rather than after the move has already priced. The other side of the initial breakout bar is whoever fades the 'overbought' print or takes first-day profit; both are wrong on average during the minority of breakouts that actually extend, which is exactly the tail this card is priced to capture and the majority that don't is exactly the cost of admission. Measured through 2026-02-13 on this ten-symbol cohort, trailing ATR(14)/price runs 6.3% (MU) to 14.0% (IREN) and the 90th-percentile absolute daily close-to-close move runs roughly 5%-12%, well above the <2% level a tight stop would need for SGOV or GLD -- stop_loss_pct and position_pct are single fixed numbers with no per-symbol scaling, so I built a universe narrow enough that one stop is a defensible approximation and left out both the cash-like names and the very calmest large-caps in the 43-symbol list. I set stop_loss_pct=0.08: above the p90 single-day move for seven of the ten names (so an ordinary bad session confirmed on the next close does not itself trigger it), but I confirmed it does sit inside normal noise for IREN, OKLO and APLD specifically (their own p90 daily moves run 10.6%-12.4%), and expect those three to be stopped out by ordinary chop more often than the rest of the book -- a mismatch I am accepting, not hiding. Simulating this exact entry against an 8% stop, 28% target and a 90-trading-day time stop over each symbol's full available history (496 qualifying, de-duplicated signals, min. 10 sessions apart): the target was reached before the stop 35.3% of the time (weighted), the stop was hit first 57.3% of the time, and only 7.5% of trades ran out the 90-day clock unresolved; measured independently of the stop, a 28%+ high was reached at some point within 90 sessions on 37.7% of signals, confirming these names do produce moves of this size often enough to be worth pricing for, not just occasionally. Median max adverse excursion across all signals was -8% to -9%, almost exactly the stop level -- ordinary pullbacks bottom close to where the stop sits, not far beyond it, which is the check the brief asks for before trusting a tight stop on daily bars. Planned reward:risk is take_profit_pct/stop_loss_pct = 0.28/0.08 = 3.5. I expect the realised ratio to fall well short of that: the 35% target-hit rate above is measured across 10-40+ years of history per name, but the trading window is a single 127-session draw, so the realistic trade count for any one name in that window is small (roughly 1-3 signals each in the design-window base rate), meaning a handful of trades will decide the whole result and the 7.5% timeout rate measured in the long sample could easily be the dominant outcome in six months if no name's breakout resolves cleanly either way before the time stop -- in which case the realised reward:risk will track the average timeout return, not 3.5, and the report's side-by-side comparison should be read with that in mind rather than as a broken plan. With a 57% base stop-first rate, expect long stretches of small losses between winners: the low win rate is not a flaw to explain away but the entire point of the payoff shape, and it means this card needs 10-20+ resolved trades before its win rate is more than noise. Position sizing (max_positions=6, position_pct=0.12, 72% max deployed) is deliberately smaller per name than a trend-following card would use, because the majority-loser payoff shape only works if no single 8% stop-out is large enough to matter, while still keeping six of ten names live so the book has enough simultaneous shots at the rare 28%+ winner.
entry: close > bb_upper(20,2) and macd_hist(12,26,9) > 0 and close > sma(50)
